## Registration lines for the lead

1. `build.sh`: add `ord_core.c ord_game.c ord_mp.c` to the source list.
2. `rig_main.c`: `#include "ord_api.h"`, and after `rig_det_install();` (after `mp_game_install();` if that is called there): `ord_install();`
3. `mp_game.c`: `#include "ord_api.h"`; after `S = mp_start(&cfg, &api, &why);` add `if (S) ord_mp_attach(S);`. Before any `mp_stop(S)`: `ord_mp_attach(NULL);`
4. Optional, `rig_det.c` `sim_cycle()`: `ord_set_ticking(1);` before the cycle body, `ord_set_ticking(0);` after (Tier B capture is already off outside UI handlers; this is a guard).

Hook budget: 22 stubs of the 80 in the rig cave. Every hook site's first instruction was checked: none is PC-relative.
If any ord hook fails, capture and replay both stay off (logged), so single player is unaffected.

## Design

- Flags: `in_interface` (set in EventQueue `b__2` / `b__3` only for events that `b__8_0` passed on as LOCAL in the last 2 frames), `executing` (ord_apply), `ticking`. Stale flags (an exception unwound through a hook) are reset on the next frame.
- Tier A (`b__8_0`): the event's class is matched against the table (classes found with `il2cpp_class_from_name`; several events have no TypeInfo slot). A command is serialized and NOT queued locally. Blocked: `ToggleConsoleRequested`, `QuickLoadRequested`, `LoadCampaignRequested`, `SaveFileRequested`. Everything else passes through and each LOCAL type is logged once (`ord: local event type X`): compare that log with catalog section 3.
- Tier A replay: rebuild the event object (no constructor; fields written, pointer stores through `il2cpp_gc_wbarrier_set_field`), swap the selection in, and run its sync handler right away by calling the same `Action<IEventData>` that `EventQueue.ProcessSyncEvent` calls (`invoke_impl(method_code, evt, method)`). If the type only has an async handler, it is queued with `AddEvent`.
- Why not `AddEvent` for sync events: the queue is drained later in the frame, after a varying number of lockstep steps, so the effect would land at a different tick on each peer.
- Tier B: the hook skips the original while `in_interface && !executing && !ticking`, then sends the args. Replay calls the original on instances found from MainFlow: `+0x50` EventHandler, then `+0x38` PlayerControlEventHandler, then `+0x20` ControlModeProcessor, then `GetProcessor(0 / 6)`, then DefaultMode `+0x18`, DefaultCommand `+0x20`, CommandFlow (`+0x10` runner, `+0x18` move, `+0x20` waypoint). Runner: `+0x18` ActionOrder, `+0x10` RunCheck, `+0x20` MoveOrder.
- Right-click on targets: `InteractionRunner.Run` is hooked as a recorder. While it runs, every `ActionOrder.Execute` is recorded and answers false, and every `MoveOrder.Near` is recorded and skipped. The replay redoes Run's choice (decompile of Run, 0xC0678C): for each unit, the first recorded candidate whose `Execute` returns true; then `Near` for units with no success. So a candidate that fails on the replay falls through to the next one, as in the game.
- Skill selectors: the factory hooks record pointer to descriptor while `in_interface`. `UseSkill` looks up its selector. If the descriptor is unknown, the order is still sent, but the replay skips it (logged).
- `DropItemRequested`: `GetRayCastPlayerEntities` is called at capture (ItemEventHandler `+0x88` reader, `_inMapDatas[evt.Map]`). Its Guid is carried, and the hook returns that unit while the replay runs.
- Tutorial `InputObserver`: becomes an order (`ORD_K_OBSERVER`), at most one per InputObserveType every 30 frames, and is dropped locally until it is replayed. The replay records it into `InputDispatcher._inputBinding._buffer`.
- Trade: `TryCommit` overwrites `request.SessionId` with this peer's `TradeHelper._sessionId` while the replay runs. The request is rebuilt with its real constructor from a `TradeCommitDelivery[]`.
- Map changes from the UI (ChangeMapRequested to Dungeon or Base, GoDownDungeonRequested) go to `ui_map_propose(kind 1|2|3, payload, len)` (dlsym; 1 = taken). The order is sent only if the ui lane is absent or returns 0. `EscapeActionRequested` stays local and never sets in_interface.
- Speed and pause events are LOCAL here on purpose: `mp_game.c` hooks `SetSpeed` / `AddPauseReason` / `RemovePauseReason` and turns them into votes. Capturing them again would double them.
- Owner Guid (mp ownership check): the event's `UserGuid` / `UnitGuid` / `Owner` / `From` / `targetGuid` / `TargetGuid` / `Guid` / `SourceGuid` / `Target`, the first that exists. For `ToggleBehaviourOption` (null Target), `ToggleTaskOptionRequested` and `SelectAmmoRequested` it is the first selected entity. For Tier B it is the first selected unit or the acting unit. Global orders (map travel, story choice) use a zero Guid.

## Only verifiable in game

1. Hooks install. The handler of each Set 1 command runs on BOTH peers with the same result (tick and world fingerprint match after: right-click move, attack, pick-up, waypoint queue, skill with target, instant skill, potion, equip / transfer / drop onto a unit, quick slots, auto-skill both ways, behaviour F/G/H, story choice, level-up roll and accept, merchant trade, next floor, return to base).
2. `PlayerControlEventHandler._selectReader` is the SelectDataContainer every handler reads. The swap is not seen by the view, and no selection leaks after a replay.
3. `InMapDataInterface.TryGetEntity` finds inventory items; if not, the ItemDataContainer fallback does.
4. The sync-delegate call is equivalent to `ProcessSyncEvent`. The skipped `IEventAdmissionGate.Release` after it is harmless for non-transition events.
5. Async commands (`ChangeMapRequested`, `GoDownDungeonRequested`, `ClearDungeonRegionRequested`, `SetSafeFloorSkip`, `SetRecentlySelectedRegion`, `QuickLoad`) run from EventQueue's coroutine, so their timing is per frame, not per step. Map travel needs a barrier (mp / det lanes). Send a forced dungeon seed.
6. Sub-events that a replayed handler adds to EventQueue (`AddEvent`) are processed later in the frame, outside the lockstep step. The det lane must drain the EventQueue at a fixed point (or the step must own it).
7. Selector rebuilt from `GridData`: a fresh GridData (Position, Flag), not the map's own object. Check that `SpecificGrid` does not compare identity.
8. `UseSkill` replay uses `GetProcessor(6)` of the current map. Check that a skill cast from `SkillOrder`'s path is not captured (it runs under `executing` in replays, and only inside `Execute`, which is skipped at capture).
9. Run recording: `Execute` answering false must have no side effect. Run must call nothing else that changes state.
10. The tutorial observer throttle (1 per type per 30 frames) does not break a trigger. If it does, turn tutorials off in multiplayer.
11. GC: objects made in replay are held by GC handles for the call. The selection list holds a permanent handle.
12. Exceptions thrown by a replayed handler unwind through C frames (same as the det lane). The flags are reset on the next frame, but the selection swap could stay until the next replay. Watch for "stale" lines in the log.

## Known gaps (not Set 1, or design decisions for the lead)

- Expedition item events (`Expedition*`) read the UI-only `ExpeditionPlanPartyContext` in their handler: base only, Set 2.
- Global single-instance helpers (`LevelUpHelper` target, `TradeHelper` session, `MapTransitionRequestGate`): two players at once collide (catalog hazard 3).
- The owner check uses one Guid. A group move with units of two owners is not filtered per unit: that belongs to the ownership step (PLAN step 4).
- `ICampaignRandomService` on the level-up roll and `Random.Range` in trade pool init belong to the det lane. They run inside `sim_scope` because `mp_core` wraps `run_order`.
- Copy and paste buffers (storage and consume policies) are Set 2.

## In-game loopback smoke, 2026-10-12 (copy C, batchmode, nice 5)

Variant build: `build_ord/build_ord.sh` (copies the rig sources, adds the registration lines and `ord_test/ord_smoke.c`),
launcher `build_ord/ord_rig.py`, helpers `build_ord/t.py`. Loopback = the emit callback queues the payload, and
`ord_apply` runs it at the start of the next frame. Actions were injected as input events through the hooked `b__8_0`.

Fixed during the smoke:
- **GC handles are pointer-sized in this il2cpp (Unity 6).** A uint32 handle crashed `il2cpp_gchandle_free` on the first Tier A replay (SIGSEGV).
- Tier A replay now calls the handler delegate's method through `il2cpp_runtime_invoke`, so a handler exception is caught (`ord: X handler threw Y`, rc -20). Before, it unwound through `ord_apply` and the rig's Update hook. A LOCAL handler that throws still unwinds through the `b__2` hook: `recover()` resets the flag on the next frame (seen once: `InteractGridRequested` threw before the hover option existed).

Batchmode limits:
- `InteractionOptionControl._registeredOption` is null until the cursor UI registers one, so right-click throws NRE in stock too. `ord_hover` registers an `InteractionOption` the same way.
- The attack quick action failed `CommandCheck.IsKnown` (fog / known check on the target), so right-click attack took the move path in stock and in loopback alike.
- `UseQuickSlotSkillRequested` did nothing in stock or loopback (no `UseSkill` call).

## Window-mode retest, 2026-10-12 (copy E, `ord_rig.py startw`, window transparent; guard: 0 kills)
- Quick-slot skill with a target click: `UseSkill` is captured as kind 9 and replayed with rc 0. The cooldown appears (`ord_read`), and the stock run behaves the same. Index 1 cast the slot-0 skill both in stock and in loopback.
- Right-click attack: still the move path in stock, because `IsEntityKnownForInteraction` (player vision) is false even next to the enemy. Replay was tested by injecting a RUN order with one attack candidate (`ord_run_attack`): rc 0, the unit enters combat (task 15) and walks to the target.
- Tier A effects read back with `ord_read` (EntityInfoComponent `+0x20`, `UnitQuickSlotContainer` quick slots, SkillComponent `_autoUse` `+0x48` and `_cooldowns` `+0x38`): quick slot unset/set/move, auto-skill toggle and behaviour toggles all changed as expected.
- Trap: `EscapeActionRequested` opens the pause menu (speed 0). Do not use it to leave skill mode.

## Set 2: base and town (2026-10-12)

Wire format v2 (`ORD_VERSION 2`). The ord table now has 85 commands + 4 blocked types (ids 52-85 are new). The 10 new hooks run on the 256+ stub table.

| Area | How it is captured | Replay detail |
|---|---|---|
| Recruit (`CandidateRecruitRequested` 52, refresh 53) | Tier A | The unit Guids on the map are compared before and after the handler. Each new unit goes to `ord_set_recruit_hook(unit, player)`; `ord_mp.c` sends `mp_assign(unit, player)` from the host (OWNERSHIP, stamped after the step). |
| Retire / rename / bed owner (54-56) | Tier A | The owner is the unit Guid (`TargetGuid` / `OwnerGuid`). |
| Crafting queue (57-62), farming (63-64) | Tier A + selection (selected station) | The selection swap carries the station. |
| Research (65-67) | Tier A | `ResearchSelectRequested` has no handler and stays local. |
| Work on/off, priority, per-unit task priority (68-70) | Tier A + selection | |
| Storage policies, copy and paste (71-76) | Tier A + selection | Copy is a command too, so there is one shared clipboard and the last copy in tick order wins. |
| Consume policies, unit copy and paste (77-83) | Tier A | |
| Remove player-owned item, lock consecration (84-85) | Tier A | |
| Build / cancel / demolish / gather / pick-up zones | Tier B, 10 hooks on `<Mode>.LeftClickInteraction` / `DragSelection` (`ORD_K_MODE_CLICK` 12 / `MODE_DRAG` 13) | The issuer's `ConstructionTargetControl` key, rotation and drag start are carried. During the call they are set on the peer's CTC; the cheat flags are forced to 0; everything is restored after. |
| Expedition item moves (26-29) | Tier A + `ORD_EF_PARTY` | The issuer's `ExpeditionPlanPartyContext` (active flag + members) is carried. During the handler, `ItemEventHandler._expeditionPlanPartyReader` (+0x68) points to a private context filled with it. |
| Equip (7, 8, 10-12, 28, 29) | `ORD_EF_EQUIP` | Before sending, every unit Guid in the event goes to `ord_set_gear_check(fn)`; 0 = blocked locally. `ord_mp.c` looks up `int mp_gear_check(const uint8_t unit[16])` with dlsym. **netcore / mpglue: export it** (host gear mode a/b/c). |

Base work is open to everyone: building, crafting and storage orders carry a zero owner (or an unowned building). Shared resources: the first order in tick order wins (the replay order is the server's).

### Rerun after the zero-owner rule (mp_core: zero Guid = global), pair AB on the rig port (7791), 23:08-23:13
The client (B) issued storage copy+paste, work toggle, crafting priority, recruit refresh, recruit and cancel click; the host issued the rest. Result: same as before, 16 PASS, and research_add fails the same way on both peers. The recruit by player 1 created unit 000002ad... on both peers. `ord_game.c` refuses to send a unit-kind order without a unit owner. An event whose owner field is empty falls back to its first unit Guid / IEntity field (or the first selected unit for selection events) before it is treated as global.

- mp_core has one zero-owner rule (`run_order`, `zero_guid`). mp_test: ALL PASS.
- Recruit by player 1: `dsnet_owner_of(new unit)` = 1 on both peers.
- Research add (save copy with RESEARCH_AdvancedStoneHousing at workload 0): replayed on both, saves equal.
- Unequip needs the unit to be SELECTED: `ItemEventHandler.CanAccessItemOwner` reads `_selectReader` (+0x60) or the expedition party. ord carries the selection, so the replay passes.
  - gear 0: own unit -> BoneHelmet moves to the inventory on both peers; host's unit -> blocked locally.
  - gear 1: host's unit -> HideHelmet moves to the inventory on both peers.
  - gear 2: same as gear 0.

### Gear mode 2: item ownership (2026-10-12, pair CD/EF, rig port)
- **Tagging** (only free items; `ord_mp.c it_tag`):
  - Bought items: new item Guids on the map after a TradeCommit replay go to the buyer, inside the replay (every peer).
  - Picked-up items: hook on `ItemEventHandler.OnEvent(PickUpItemRequested)` 0xDA0830. The item goes to the unit's owner; the host sends ITEM_OWNER.
  - Crafted items: the replay of `CraftingTaskGenerateRequested` records station -> issuer. The hook on `TaskFinishEventHandler.TryCraft` 0xDCA568 diffs the map's item Guids and the host tags the new ones.
- **Check**: the item an event takes is read from the holder's `InventoryComponent._itemSlots[slot]` (ItemHolder.Guid). The table is `item_src` in ord_game.c. TransferStorage uses `SourceGuid` + `SlotIndex` (0x38); its `Index` (0x14) is the selection index. The capture blocks it locally, and the replay drops it on every peer (rc -30) when `dsnet_may_use_item(issuer, item)` is 0. `UseSkill` with an item is checked the same way.
- **Proven**:
  - Crafted dish 00000402 -> player 1 on both peers (client queued it).
  - Client takes its own tagged ClothArmor from equipment storage: storage slot 0 empty and ClothArmor in f173's inventory on both peers, saves equal.
  - Client tries the host's BoneSpear: blocked locally, storage unchanged.
- Gear 1/2 item changes in the save: see "Gaps closed" above (HideHelmet / BoneHelmet moved).
- **Not proven in game**: the pickup tag and the trade-buy tag (no ground item / merchant staged). Also unchecked: whether an item keeps its Guid (and so its tag) after a move storage -> inventory, and what happens to a split or merged stack (a new Guid would make it free).

### "All units" orders follow ownership (owner live feedback, 2026-10-13)
- Replay filter (`may_order`): the swapped-in selection, the RUN candidate units and the near-move units keep only the units the issuer may order (own units; unclaimed units only for the host). The rule reads dsnet's ownership table, so every peer agrees. It covers select-all + move / waypoint / right-click, behaviour options with no target, task options (pick-up / gather on/off for the selection) and auto-skill.
- Pick-up designations (PickUpMode, shared tasks that any worker takes): the replay records the click / drag area per issuer. The hook on `TaskAssignableHelper.IsAvailable` 0xAE5038 refuses PickUp tasks (TaskType 101) whose item lies in another player's area. Areas are in memory only, so after a reload old designations are free.
- Other shared designations (build, demolish, cancel, gather) stay open to everyone: base work.
- Proof, pair IJ, dungeon save, gear 0. B (client) owns Leo and Silvarion; the host owns Ivan and Leonis (unclaimed).
  - The host drops Ivan's WoodClub (443,104). The client designates a pick-up there: the host's units are refused on both peers (log), Silvarion picks the club up; inventories, saves and fingerprints are equal.
  - The client selects all and right-clicks: Leo and Silvarion move, Ivan and Leonis stay, on both peers.
